::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
CEC's (China Electronics Corporation) manufacturing anchor and China's flagship state-owned car-grade specialty foundry — a ¥35.9 billion Lingang complex (groundbreaking August 2018) merged with the legacy Shanghai Advanced (SAS) semiconductor plant, plus an ¥8 billion November 2021 strategic round featuring automaker (SAIC), industrial (Inovance) and Xiaomi supply-chain investors.
:::

**Chinese name:** 上海积塔半导体有限公司 (Shànghǎi Jītǎ Bàndǎotǐ Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

Automotive/industrial MCU, BCD analog/PMIC, IGBT/MOSFET and sensor wafers; company capacity pages report 8-inch output above 1.3 million wafers/year, with the 12-inch line (planned ~500,000 wafers/year at full capacity) still marked under construction/ramping.

## Why does it matter?

One of the very few dedicated car-grade 12-inch lines in China and one of the few domestic SiC (6-inch) and FeRAM/eNVM capability holders — a key supply node if China's domestic car-MCU push continues; still private (named a national 'unicorn' in 2026); no verified IPO filing as of this pass.

## Project Timeline

- **Aug 2018** — ¥35.9 billion Lingang specialty-process line breaks ground; merger with legacy Shanghai Advanced Semiconductor agreed
- **Nov 2021** — ¥8 billion strategic financing completed, led by Huada Semiconductor (CEC)
- **Jun 2023** — 12-inch line activated (tool line-out)
- **Dec 2025** — Wins 'Influential SiC Wafer Manufacturing Service' at the行家极光 awards
